questions.q: How much heat does a linear BEC dissipate with 25 V in, 5 V out and 0.5 A of current?
questions.explain: (25 − 5) V × 0.5 A = 10 W — a linear regulator dumps the entire voltage difference as heat.

questions.q: Why put a low-ESR capacitor on the power bus?
options: To absorb spikes caused by inductance
Reverse-polarity protection for the battery connector
questions.explain: U = L·dI/dt when the ESC switches: the capacitor acts as a local source and clips the spikes.

questions.q: What voltage margin should the capacitor have on 6S (25.2 V fully charged)?
questions.explain: Margin ≥ 30%: for 6S use 50 V; 35 V is for 4S.

questions.explain: A bulb or a resistor in series with the positive lead at the first power-up after soldering: on a short the bulb lights up and the aircraft doesn't smoke.

questions.q: Why is a voltage sag dangerous for the FC?
options: The BEC shuts off — the FC resets
questions.explain: Buck converters have a minimum input voltage; a sag below it restarts the board.

questions.q: What happens to a connector that's overloaded for the current?
options: It reduces the ripple on the power bus
questions.explain: Heating → oxidation → rising resistance → even more heating.

questions.q: Which BEC is better for powering the receiver and the sensitive RF part?
questions.explain: An LDO produces no ripple; a buck → LDO chain gives both efficiency and a clean supply.

questions.q: A Raspberry Pi on board reboots during maneuvers. In dmesg:
questions.fragment:
[  812.4] hwmon hwmon1: Undervoltage detected!
[  812.9] hwmon hwmon1: Voltage normalised
Power: 5 V / 1 A BEC from the flight controller
options: A 1 A BEC can't handle a Pi (up to 2–3 A): it sags on peaks — you need a separate 5 V / 5 A BEC
The CPU is overheating: hwmon is reporting throttling, not voltage
The memory card is damaged, and the kernel misinterprets write failures as a sag
The message is routine: a Pi always logs it when Wi-Fi starts and it can be ignored
questions.explain: The Pi itself reports the sag; the on-board 5 V from the FC is meant for light loads.
